chapter_theme: Jnana, the fourth and highest path: there is no dharma, religion or release above it. Its marks are going beyond sound and the faculties, loss of 'I' and 'mine', passing beyond merit and sin, and becoming the pure, freed Siva-siddha. Like yoga, jnana has the four paths within it and four grades, ending at the good guru's feet.
structure_note: Jnana's supremacy (1467), what the knower passes beyond (1468 to 1471), an obscure symbolic verse (1472), the paths within jnana (1473, 1474), the knower described (1475) and jnana's four grades (1476), matching 1450 and 1466.

1467.reading: There is no path of dharma in the land higher than jnana, no religion beyond jnana is good, what goes beyond jnana does not give good release, and those who excel in jnana excel among men.
1467.nuance: ஞானத்தின் மிக்க opens every line, but its sense shifts: in the first three it is 'higher than jnana', in the last 'abounding in jnana'. The verse ranks dharma and religion below jnana without rejecting them.

1468.reading: Sound and reflection on sound, the fitting mind, directed awareness, the ego that makes aware, and these three with the chitta, and the act of thinking itself: going beyond sound, those who pass them gain the true path.
1468.nuance: The list looks like the inner instruments (manas, buddhi, ahankara, chitta), with சத்தம் and சத்த மனனம் perhaps standing for hearing and reflecting on teaching (sravana, manana). How the items group into 'these three' is unclear. சன்மார்க்கம் here is the path of jnana, the subject of the next chapter.

1469.reading: That the world is in him and what is near him, and what becomes grace to me through love: those who can say these gain jnana, reach Sivoham, and receive the love that follows.
1469.nuance: சிவோகம் (I am Siva) is a contemplative formula of identity. The first two lines are compressed and the subject of தன்பால் (in himself) may be the Lord or the knower. The verse has love both before jnana (அன்பால்) and after it (பின்பாலின் நேயம்).

1470.reading: For those who have examined and understood the jnana without crookedness, the safe place to dwell is Brahman, all classes of being make up the moving and unmoving world, and it gives the fruit of all the proud observances.
1470.nuance: திருக்கிலா ஞானம் is jnana without twist or crookedness. தருக்கிய ஆசாரம் may be observances that people take pride in, or observances that are reasoned out; the claim is that jnana yields what they aim at. The grammar of the first two lines is loose.

1471.reading: The greatly gracious one dwells in the city that knowledge, restraint and love never leave; his sign, his qualities and his sounding feet do not leave it; for those who know the way, this is plain as the sound of water.
1471.nuance: The 'city' (நகர்) is probably the knower's own heart or body. நீர்த்தொனி (the sound of water) is obscure; it may mean something clearly heard, or something heard in still water. The pairing of knowledge, restraint and love is the verse's clear teaching.

1472.reading: In a mind where jnana ripens and rises, a boar springs up to be seen ahead at every turn; seeing the water facing the curved moon's circle, cutting off all defect, one stands as a bright flame.
1472.nuance: ஏனம் (boar) may recall Vishnu as the boar who dug for Siva's foot, or ஏனம் may mean a vessel; கூனல் மதி மண்டலம் (the circle of the bent moon) and the water before it are traditionally the moon-region in the head and its nectar. The ending is plain: defect cut away, the knower becomes light. The rest is symbolic and I can't fix it.

1473.reading: For the jnani the four are in jnana with its qualities; for the silent one none of these join; before that, deluded, Shakti stands above and makes knowledge grow; those of this kind are of chariyai and kiriyai.
1473.nuance: The verse seems to grade the jnani, for whom the four paths are within jnana, above the silent one (மோனி) who is past all of them, and below both those still in chariyai and kiriyai. The middle lines (மோகித்து மேல் நிற்றல் ஆம் சத்தி வித்தை) are obscure.

1474.reading: For the jnani the four beginning with jnana are within jnana: jnana in jnana is not saying 'I' and 'mine'; yoga in jnana is the good light at the end of nada; kiriyai in jnana is seeking good release.
1474.nuance: Each path is said to contain all four (jnana in jnana, yoga in jnana and so on); the verse gives three of the four within jnana and leaves out chariyai. நாதாந்தம் (the end of nada) is technical. The clearest line is the first: jnana's own core is the end of 'I' and 'mine'.

1475.reading: He who reaches jnana-in-jnana has passed beyond merit and sin, is free of strife, has seen the beloved jnana of the far shore, and is the firm, pure, Siva-freed siddha.
1475.nuance: புண்ணிய பாவம் கடந்த says the knower is beyond both good and bad deeds, not only bad ones. கரைஞானம் (shore-jnana) may be the knowledge of the far shore or the knowledge at the limit; கண்ணிய நேயம் (the cherished, or the intended, object of love) is unclear.

1476.reading: Jnana-samaya is seeing the self one seeks; jnana-visesha is the rising of the Supreme one seeks; jnana-nirvana is the grace of the one who knows the good; jnana-abhisheka is the good guru's feet.
1476.nuance: நற்குறு பாதம் is read as நற்குரு பாதம், the good guru's feet. The sequence runs from seeing the self, to the Supreme rising, to grace, to the guru's feet: the summit of jnana is placed at the guru.

links.note: The Kural asks what gain is greater than aram, which yields distinction and wealth; Tirumular says no path of aram is higher than jnana. They conflict only if the Kural's aram is meant to rank above liberating knowledge; Tirumular keeps aram but places it below jnana.
Both set the cutting off of 'I' and 'mine' at the summit: the Kural says whoever cuts that pride enters a world above the gods', Tirumular makes it jnana within jnana itself.
Both free the one who knows or praises the Lord from both kinds of deed: the Kural's twofold deeds of darkness do not cling to him, Tirumular's knower has passed beyond merit and sin alike.
The same four grades are applied to yoga and to jnana; yoga's summit is siddhi (1466), jnana's is the good guru's feet (1476).

Tirumanthiram 1468 lists sound, reflection, mind, awareness, ego and chitta, and says those who go beyond them gain the true path. Tirumanthiram 2153 says that once the five senses, their objects and the four inner instruments (உண்டன நான்கும்) are understood together, the soul becomes as it was of old. Both make passing through the inner instruments the step to the soul's own state; 2153 sets it in the doctrine of the states (அவத்தை).

Tirumanthiram 1469 says those who can speak of the world in him and the grace that comes through love gain jnana and reach Sivoham (சிவோகம், 'I am Siva'). Tirumanthiram 2403 calls the abiding So'ham (சோகம்) the crowning Siva-yoga of the knowers of the Veda and the meaning of the Siddhanta. 1469 gives the identity formula as the fruit of jnana; 2403 places the same formula at the head of Veda and Agama alike.

Kural 123 says that restraint (அடங்க), recognised as knowledge (அறிவறிந்து), yields distinction. Tirumanthiram 1471 names knowledge, restraint and love (அறிவும் அடக்கமும் அன்பும்) as never parting from the city where the gracious Lord dwells. The Kural joins knowledge and restraint for worldly honour; Tirumular adds love and makes the three together the Lord's dwelling.

Tirumanthiram 1473 seems to rank the jnani and the silent one above those of chariyai and kiriyai (சரியை கிரியையே), the lower class. Thiruppugazh 1157 says the reality is far from those infatuated with chariyai, kiriyai, sacrifice and yoga (சரியை கிரியைமக யோக மோகிகள்). Both set the ritual and yogic paths below the knowing of the goal, though 1473's grammar is too compressed to fix in detail.

source_issues: 1476: நற்குறு பாதம் is probably நற்குரு பாதம்.
1472 is symbolic and obscure throughout (ஏனம், கூனல் மதி மண்டலம்); some words may be corrupt.
